title: My AI-assisted Unity workflow uses a scene builder. Where do you draw the line with the Inspector?
author: ApartmentWest6722
selftext:
I've been using Claude and Codex on my Android game Gravewave. One part of the workflow is a C# editor script that rebuilds the base scene and the prefabs it needs.

The menu command creates a fresh scene, sets up the camera and lighting, generates unit and building prefabs, and saves the scene. The 3D models come from KayKit; the script assembles and configures them.

That puts the setup in code the coding tools can inspect and edit. But it also creates a boundary: if I change a generated object only in the Inspector, rebuilding can overwrite that change. Anything meant to survive needs to be represented in the builder or in source assets it reads.

I still need to open Unity and check the result. Compiling the builder doesn't tell me whether the camera framing, materials, or unit scale look right.

For anyone using coding agents with Unity: which parts of scene and prefab setup do you generate, and which do you keep hand-authored? I'm especially interested in how you keep designers' Inspector edits from getting lost on rebuild.

For context, the project also uses some AI-generated UI illustrations; the 3D assets are KayKit.
